dedupe_keys.name: global mining areas targeting materials critical for renewable energy production and other materials sonter et al 2020

description: Three global 1 km rasters of 'mine density' made for Sonter et al. (2020), "Renewable energy production will exacerbate mining threats to biodiversity", Nature Communications. The figshare record says the maps count, for each cell, the mining properties within a 50-cell radius, using 62,381 pre-operational, operational and closed properties that target 40 commodities, taken from S&P Global Market Intelligence (2018). Separate maps show Critical Mining Areas (materials needed for renewable energy), Other Mining Areas (for example fossil fuels and fertilisers) and areas in both groups. The record was created on 9 July 2020 and last modified on 2 September 2020 by Laura Sonter; it holds GeoTIFF files with overviews and attribute tables, about 35 MB in all, free under CC BY 4.0, in Mollweide equal-area projection. Caveats: the maps show density of properties, not disturbed area, the underlying S&P property list is commercial and not shared, and the 50-cell radius is a modelling choice for indirect impacts. For simulation it gives a global exposure layer of where mining for energy-transition materials concentrates, to overlay with hazard, water or biodiversity layers when studying supply risk. Related catalogue records include the Maus global mining polygons and the Global Tailings Portal.
